A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COPE with matching methods and benchmark experiments. All 18 pages of v1 and 21 pages of v2, including appendices, tables, equations, and rendered figures, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original personalized-generation experiments on five tasks, including baseline comparisons, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: V2 retains those experiments and adds original reward-validation, extended-ablation, perplexity, and instance-level analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: Both retain LoRA personalization, plausibility-constrained contrastive decoding, and DPO using lowest-reward synthetic negatives (Equations 1–6). Figure 2's corrections align its illustration with the already stated procedure; the added validation does not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both use Abstract Generation, Review Writing, Topic Writing, News Headline, and Scholarly Title from LaMP/LongLaMP. V2 explains task exclusions in Appendix A and analyzes retained data more extensively, without adding a dataset, task, or distinct population.

E2.justification: The main baseline comparisons remain unchanged. However, Table 9 newly evaluates CD-only and DPO-only comparators on Review Writing, Topic Writing, and Scholarly Title; v1 reported these variants only for Abstract Generation and News Headline in Table 3.

E3.justification: V2 adds substantial diagnostic protocols: reward comparisons using 10 randomly selected users and 20% history samples, perplexity evaluation with a common reference model, and instance-level comparisons against TAM with task macro-averaging. The existing benchmark split, training budgets, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendices D–G test whether reward ratios distinguish users, extend component ablations from two tasks to all five, examine perplexity and fluency, and investigate whether average gains conceal uneven instance-level performance. Figure 4 also adds a second headline case; the original sensitivity analyses and appendix examples are retained.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's point performance estimates and dataset statistics, v2 reports perplexity standard deviations and ROUGE standard errors across test samples, with a 95% confidence-interval discussion in Appendix H. This introduces performance uncertainty reporting, but does not document repeated training runs or additional seeds.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical entries, while v2 adds extensive diagnostic results. Table 8 reports mean own-user versus other-user rewards of 0.095 versus 0.026; Table 9 reveals Topic Writing ROUGE-L of 0.122 for CD alone versus 0.120 for full COPE. Section 4.2 corrects the LaMP relative gain from 3.89% to 1.95%. New COPE mean ROUGE-L summaries conflict between Tables 9 and 12: 0.230 versus 0.228.

T1.justification: The formal definitions, Equations 1–6, and RLHF/DPO derivations are retained, with the background moved from Appendix F to Appendix I. The new support for the reward proxy is empirical rather than a new theorem, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: decoding-time personalization through implicit rewards, synthetic-negative preference training, no external reward model, and applicability across tasks and LLMs. The headline 10.57% and 5.67% ROUGE-L improvement claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations of reward ratios as user-specific signals, perplexity versus personalization, informal gold-text predictability, user heterogeneity, and statistical reliability. It also attributes weaker combined ablation results on Topic Writing to potentially suboptimal uniform hyperparameters. The existing general limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies sampling details for reward validation, identifies Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 as the perplexity reference model, and reports task-specific test-instance totals in Table 11. Existing optimization hyperparameters and the code-access statement are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction adds Kim et al. (2025b) on privacy-preserving evolutionary model merging and Zhang et al. (2025a) on parameterized memory injection. The additional Tan et al. (2025) reference repeats the already cited Tan et al. (2024) work. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language edits, revises the limitations and ethics wording, updates affiliations/contact information, and adds acknowledgments. It preserves the main narrative while moving prompts and chat templates behind quantitative analyses and RLHF/DPO background, with corresponding appendix-reference updates.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 8–13 and Figure 5, expands Figure 4 to two headline examples with boxed token matches, and redraws Figures 1–2. Figure 2 correctly highlights −0.103 rather than −0.045 as the minimum and displays the existing contrastive weight. Retained appendix displays are relocated; Table 13 redisplays averages from Table 11.

improvement.justification: The full-task ablations make component effects clearer, including Topic Writing's CD-only advantage, while the corrected LaMP percentage and Figure 2 improve accuracy. These provide a modest net gain in transparency. The benefit is limited by new reporting problems: conflicting mean ROUGE-L summaries, Appendix F's perplexity bound contradicting Table 10, and Appendix H claiming statistical reliability without establishing significance of performance differences.
